findings.claim: The new staging makes the deployed done-when impossible to pass. 1.14 must run tests (1), (3), (4), (6) and (7) with the kill switch on, but while the switch is on every turn gets the offline state and there is no bypass. The switch only turns off after 1.14 passes, so the plan deadlocks.
findings.evidence: site-spend-ceiling/tasks.md:41 (1.14): "runs after the first deploy, with the kill switch on: re-run tests (1), (3), (4), (6) and (7) against the deployed stack ... Then the operator turns the kill switch off." tasks.md:29 (1.9): the switch "returns the offline state on every replica". github-deploy-workflows/tasks.md:9 (1.7): "no public chat turn can reach UAR ... There is no bypass." Every test 1.14 lists needs a turn to reach UAR: (1) settles from `agui.done`, (3) and (7) need turns "admitted", and (6) needs the total to cross 80% and exhaustion through settled usage. The parent plan (plan.md:85) and the critical path (plan.md:90) chain: N15 1.14 → switch off → E11 1.5/1.4 → N21 → exit. 09-implementation-plan.md:50 says the same: "re-verified on the deployed stack with the kill switch on; then the operator turns the switch off." Two outcomes follow. Either Phase 0 cannot exit, or the operator turns the switch off before the meter is proven, which defeats the reason for staging (prior finding W7).
findings.suggested_fix: Define a test path that passes the kill switch only for an operator-held credential or source (an allowlisted header carrying a Secret, or a port-forward that is not routed through the gateway) and record it as a named exception to 1.7's "no bypass" rule. Alternatively, state that 1.14 runs with the switch off while the global route sits at 0 replicas or behind an IP allowlist. Make the same correction in github-deploy-workflows 1.7, plan.md step 8 and §9's staging sentence.

findings.claim: The reservation transaction depends on a conditional UPDATE 'failing' and cancelling the transaction. In SurrealQL, an UPDATE whose WHERE matches no row is not an error: it returns an empty result and the transaction commits. When the daily row fits but the monthly row does not, the daily reservation commits and leaks.
findings.evidence: tasks.md:11-12: "Each row is updated only `WHERE total + n <= budget`. If either conditional update fails, the transaction is cancelled and the turn is refused". No task requires an explicit check (`IF` on the result count, then `THROW`/`CANCEL`). The stack pins SurrealDB v3.3.0 (plan.md:119). If the implementation follows the text, the turn is refused, but the counter that fit keeps n. Each refused turn then inflates that counter, so once the monthly budget is exhausted the daily counter fills with phantom reservations. Done-when (3) and (7) do not test a mixed daily-fits/monthly-full case, so this would surface only as unexplained early daily exhaustion in production.
findings.suggested_fix: Specify the mechanism: inside BEGIN…COMMIT, run each conditional UPDATE with RETURN, check that it changed exactly one row, and THROW otherwise so the whole transaction is cancelled. Add a done-when case: monthly full and daily not full means the turn is refused and neither counter changes.

findings.claim: The reservation size n is defined from UAR `max_tokens_per_turn`, but no task sets that limit. It is not set anywhere in the repo, so UAR applies no per-turn check and n has no defined value. The excess fixture in done-when (3) also contradicts 1.8's own claim that n covers the largest turn.
findings.evidence: tasks.md:28 (1.8) sets only `max_output_tokens`, then defines "n = `max_tokens_per_turn` plus one model call's maximum". `grep -rn max_tokens_per_turn uar/ k8s/ docker-compose.yaml server/` returns nothing, and `uar/agents/knowme-site.json` has no budget. UAR's `check_limits` (origin/main `src/uar/runtime/cost_budget.rs:292-306`) applies the Run token limit only when `limits.max_tokens_per_turn` is Some: it bails when `tokens + reserved >= limit`. When the limit is None, nothing bounds a run. If the limit is set, that same check bounds a run at (limit − 1) plus one call, which 1.8's n already covers. But 1.3 (tasks.md:16) says usage can exceed n "by up to one call", and 1.12(3) (tasks.md:35) requires "a multi-call run whose actual usage exceeds n". Under 1.8's sizing that run cannot be built honestly, so test (3) would be passed with an artificially small n that is not the production n.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a task that sets `max_tokens_per_turn` (and `max_tool_calls_per_turn`) in the knowme-site agent artifact and records the value. Restate 1.3's excess cause as the cases n does not cover (for example parallel sub-calls or remote children), or drop the claim. Let test (3) use a deliberately reduced test n and say so.

findings.claim: Prior W3 is fixed in the tasks but not in the paper or the proposal. §4.8, §9 and the proposal still say the budget cannot be overshot and that the reservation is a single daily UPDATE. That contradicts tasks 1.2 and 1.3, which use a two-counter transaction and charge excess that can push a counter past its budget.
findings.evidence: 04-architecture.md:348: "Concurrent turns reserve before they run, so the budget cannot be overshot." 04-architecture.md:350: "The reservation is one atomic `UPDATE … SET total += n WHERE total + n <= budget`." 09-implementation-plan.md:50: "concurrent turns cannot overshoot the budget", and its done-when lists only (1)–(6), with no rollover and no excess alert. site-spend-ceiling/proposal.md:7: "concurrent turns cannot overshoot"; proposal.md:9: "The reservation is one atomic `UPDATE …`". Against these, tasks.md:16: "That can take a counter past its budget". FR-36 (08-functional-spec.md:187) and §6.4 item 4 (06-security-privacy.md:90) still reserve `max_tokens_per_turn` rather than 1.8's n and omit the excess alert. The child plan's N15 row (plan.md:61) does carry the 'bounded and measured, not zero' wording, so the sources now disagree with each other.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace 'cannot be overshot' with the bounded-and-measured statement in §4.8, §9 and the proposal. Describe the transaction over daily and monthly rows in §4.8 and the proposal. Add (7) and the excess alert to the §9 done-when, FR-36 and §6.4 item 4, then reassemble agent-led-site.md.

findings.claim: Scope narrowed without saying so. 1.14 makes deployed tests (2) and (5) optional (operator approval), but the child plan, the parent plan and §9 all say the done-when must pass on the deployed stack before the ceiling counts toward Phase 0 exit.
findings.evidence: tasks.md:41: "Tests (2) and (5) can run there only if the operator approves", and no outcome is defined if approval is withheld. Child plan, final paragraph: "N15's done-when (1)–(6) ... must pass on the deployed stack before the spend ceiling counts toward Phase 0 exit." 09-implementation-plan.md:50: "These run on the deployed stack before the ceiling counts toward Phase 0 exit". Parent plan.md:101: "Its six done-when tests on the deployed stack are its first independent check." Test (5), fail-closed, is the property the design calls essential ("A ceiling that fails open is not a ceiling", child plan N15), and it would never be proven where it matters.
findings.suggested_fix: Make deployed (5) mandatory using the non-destructive method 1.12 already names (revoke the meter credential, or a NetworkPolicy cutting knowme-web → SurrealDB only), which takes nothing from UAR down. Or record an explicit operator-accepted exception and update the child plan, the parent plan and §9 to match.

findings.claim: The kill switch that first-deploy safety depends on has no manifest owner. No task adds or mounts its ConfigMap in `k8s/`, and the deploy re-applies all of `k8s/` on every push. An operator's emergency flip made with kubectl is reverted by the next commit to main, or, if the ConfigMap is not in git, the switch's default state is undefined.
findings.evidence: `grep -rni kill.switch k8s` returns nothing. k8s-stack-manifests 1.6 (tasks.md:8) adds only the NetworkPolicy and the meter Secret reference, and its gate 1.4 (tasks.md:6) checks neither a kill-switch ConfigMap nor its volume mount. `.github/workflows/site.yml:137`: `kubectl kustomize k8s | kubectl apply -f -` runs on every push to main. site-spend-ceiling 1.9 says only "reads it from a mounted ConfigMap file". github-deploy-workflows 1.7 requires the switch to be **on** at first deploy, but nothing defines where that 'on' value lives or who changes it.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a k8s-stack-manifests task: a ConfigMap with the switch defaulting to on, mounted into knowme-web, checked by gate 1.4. State whether the switch is changed by a git commit (CI-applied) or kept outside kustomize (operator-only, so `apply` never overwrites it), and test that a redeploy does not change its value.

findings.claim: Stale cross-references point to the wrong gate after site-agent-seed was renumbered. kb-chunking-quality and the parent plan still say site-agent-seed 1.3 holds the deployed FR-8 check, but 1.3 is now the local gate and the deployed check is 1.6.
findings.evidence: kb-chunking-quality/proposal.md:10: "The deployed FR-8 check belongs to `site-agent-seed` 1.3"; kb-chunking-quality/tasks.md:9 (1.7): "The deployed FR-8 check is `site-agent-seed` 1.3". Parent plan.md:24 (E7): "1.3 runs after `kb-chunking-quality` and holds the deployed FR-8 check". Child plan, review-response table: "the deployed FR-8 check belongs to `site-agent-seed` 1.3". In fact site-agent-seed/tasks.md:5 says "Integration gate against the **local** stack", and tasks.md:8 (1.6) is the "Deployed gate". The reopen-on-failure contract between the two changes is therefore anchored to a local check.

findings.claim: Canonical KBD state was not re-synced after the tasks.md fixes. The canonical task text for site-spend-ceiling and kb-chunking-quality is the pre-fix version, and the gate-before-new-task ordering means the projection names the github-deploy-workflows gate as the next task.
findings.evidence: `prometheus kbd --path . status --json`, site-spend-ceiling: 1.4 "Add the monthly token budget (D-3) to the same meter and the same atomic reservation"; 1.6 "Alerts: fire a warning at 80% of the daily budget and an alert at exhaustion" (no monthly or excess alert); 1.12 "Done-when: run tests (1)–(6)". tasks.md has (1)–(7), a transaction and an excess alert. kb-chunking-quality canonical 1.6 still reads "File the UAR default-chunker fix", although tasks.md:8 was reworded to wait on D-12 (prior S14). progress.json github-deploy-workflows: "next_task_pending": "Gate: a green `main` run end to end...", because canonical sequence 4 (the gate) precedes 1.5–1.7. Prior W11 was addressed only by 'run after' prose, which a sequence-driven executor does not read. The same applies to k8s-stack-manifests (gate at sequence 4, before 1.5 and 1.6).
findings.suggested_fix: Re-register the edited task titles in canonical KBD and re-sequence the three amended changes so that each gate is last in canonical order. Re-project progress.json.

findings.claim: Settlement does not say which period's rows it adjusts. A turn reserved before a UTC day or month boundary and settled after it either changes the new period's row (crediting the unused reservation to the wrong day) or needs the reservation's period keys, and no task says to carry them.
findings.evidence: tasks.md:14 (1.3): "adjust both counters by `usage.total_tokens − n` in one transaction". tasks.md:9 keys rows by UTC period. tasks.md:40 (1.13): "The previous period's row is kept ... and not reused." Test (7) (tasks.md:39) checks only that the first turn after the boundary is admitted, not a turn that straddles it.
findings.suggested_fix: Have the reservation return its day and month record ids, and settle against exactly those rows. Add a straddling-turn case to test (7).

findings.claim: The pre-deploy staging omits 1.10 (FR-38 records), but the local done-when it requires before the first deploy needs those records.
findings.evidence: tasks.md:4: "Before the first deploy: tasks 1.1–1.9 and 1.13, with the local done-when (1.12) passing". 1.12(3) (tasks.md:35) requires "The resulting overshoot equals the recorded excess", and 1.3 (tasks.md:17) says excess "is recorded (1.10)".
